prompt.brief: Design a semantic search engine that indexes versioned documents, combines lexical and vector retrieval, reranks results by relevance, enforces access control, and supports fresh updates at large scale.
successSignals: Define document/tenant/ACL identity, chunking, embedding/model versions, lexical and vector indexes, freshness, ranking, and deletion semantics.
Combine keyword and ANN candidates, rerank with bounded work, preserve citations, filter unauthorized documents before display, and handle empty/ambiguous queries.
Separate ingestion and index builds from serving; publish atomic snapshots, support incremental updates, replay, rollback, and multi-region reads.
Explain relevance evaluation, poisoning/prompt risks, privacy, hot queries, observability, and lexical fallback when vector search fails.

functional: Ingest and parse documents, create versioned chunks/embeddings and lexical indexes, and publish searchable snapshots.
Accept natural-language and keyword queries, retrieve/rerank authorized results, return highlights/citations, filters, scores, and index freshness.
Support document updates/deletion, ACL changes, synonyms, evaluation sets, backfills, index rollback, and degraded lexical search.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 query latency under 100ms for common searches and expose recall/relevance and freshness metrics.
Scale to 100M documents and 10k queries per second without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

architecture.title: Ai Powered Semantic Search Engine search architecture
architecture.summary: Design a semantic search engine that indexes versioned documents, combines lexical and vector retrieval, reranks results by relevance, enforces access control, and supports fresh updates at large scale. The design keeps canonical source versions and access policy separate from versioned lexical/vector indexes, then uses bounded retrieval, explainable ranking, and generation-aware caching.

layers.label: Search request plane
layers.description: Authenticated clients receive bounded, tenant-authorized query and suggestion responses.

layers.label: Source and indexing plane
layers.description: Canonical documents, source versions, and index generations support replay and atomic rebuilds.

layers.label: Retrieval and relevance plane
layers.description: Candidate retrieval and ranking combine lexical, vector, freshness, and product-specific signals.

layers.label: Search quality and operations
layers.description: Freshness, relevance, latency, and access-control correctness are measured continuously.

keyPaths.label: Query serving path
keyPaths.description: Client -> gateway -> query understanding -> index -> ranker -> ACL-aware cache -> client.

keyPaths.label: Source indexing path
keyPaths.description: Source -> ingestion -> canonical document store -> versioned index generation.

components.label: Search and suggestion clients
components.description: Users submit queries, typeahead prefixes, filters, and pagination requests and receive relevance and freshness metadata.

components.label: Search API gateway
components.description: Authenticates callers, applies tenant and query quotas, normalizes language and filters, and routes reads separately from indexing.

components.label: Query understanding service
components.description: Tokenizes and expands queries, applies spelling or semantic interpretation, validates filters, and creates a bounded retrieval plan.

properties.latency: Bounded query plan and timeout budget

components.label: Document and source ingestion
components.description: Fetches or accepts source changes, extracts searchable fields, applies ACLs and deduplication, and emits versioned index work.

properties.guarantee: Source version and ACL validation before indexing

components.label: Document and source store
components.description: Retains canonical documents, crawl/import metadata, ACL snapshots, and source versions for reindexing and audit.

properties.retention: Immutable versions with source and access policy lineage

components.label: Inverted and vector index
components.description: Indexes token, field, facet, and embedding representations with tenant and ACL filters and atomic generation aliases.

properties.indexing: Versioned shards and atomic alias swap

components.label: Relevance and ranking service
components.description: Combines lexical, semantic, freshness, popularity, personalization, and business rules while recording explainable ranking features.

properties.ranking: Timeout-bounded ranking with safe lexical fallback

components.label: Query and suggestion cache
components.description: Caches normalized query results and prefixes with ACL-aware keys, short TTLs, and generation invalidation after index updates.

components.label: Search quality and operations
components.description: Tracks indexing lag, freshness, zero-result rate, relevance quality, ACL leaks, shard health, cache hit rate, and query tail latency.

properties.alerts: Stale index, query tail, quality, and authorization failures

connections.label: Query or suggestion
connections.description: Clients send a bounded query, filters, cursor, locale, and caller context through the authenticated API.

connections.label: Normalized retrieval plan
connections.description: The gateway validates ACL context, quota, and query size before query understanding selects the retrieval strategy.

connections.label: Lexical or vector retrieval
connections.description: The query service retrieves tenant-authorized candidates with a timeout and index-generation watermark.

connections.label: Candidate documents
connections.description: The ranker receives bounded candidates, fields, facets, and retrieval scores for final ordering.

connections.label: Ranked result
connections.description: Ranked pages or suggestions are cached only with tenant, ACL, query normalization, and index generation in the key.

connections.label: Search response
connections.description: The client receives results, facets, cursors, relevance metadata, and a freshness indicator or explicit timeout fallback.

connections.label: Canonical source version
connections.description: Ingestion writes the source document and import metadata before creating an indexable version.

connections.label: Indexing work
connections.description: Workers extract fields and embeddings, deduplicate versions, and publish changes for partition-local indexing.

connections.label: Index freshness and health
connections.description: Operations observes ingestion-to-index delay, shard failures, ACL filtering, generation swaps, and reindex progress.

connections.label: Query quality and latency
connections.description: Query telemetry reports tail latency, zero results, cache behavior, ranking outcomes, and privacy-safe quality samples.

deepDives.title: ACL correctness and index generations
points: Filter ai powered semantic search engine results by tenant and effective ACL, or prove the active generation contains the same policy snapshot.
Build shadow generations and swap aliases atomically so partial reindexes are never visible.
Keep source versions and ACL snapshots for replay when permissions or content change.

deepDives.title: Latency, cursors, and graceful degradation
points: Use bounded candidate retrieval, stable sort keys, and generation-aware cursors for ai powered semantic search engine pagination.
Serve the last healthy generation when a new build is incomplete, but expose freshness and avoid silently violating authorization.
Protect the query path with timeouts, circuit breakers, and per-tenant quotas.

deepDives.title: Relevance feedback without leakage
points: Separate ai powered semantic search engine click or conversion signals from personally identifying data and honor retention or deletion requests.
Evaluate ranking by query class and tail latency, not only aggregate click-through.
Use replayable query sets and staged model or synonym changes before production rollout.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous indexing versus queued indexing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Commit the source version synchronously and index asynchronously with a visible freshness contract.
tradeoffs.caution: Waiting for index mutation makes writes fragile and cannot guarantee immediate consistency at scale.

tradeoffs.title: Denormalized ACL fields versus filter-time checks
tradeoffs.recommendation: Denormalize safe, versioned authorization facts when it meets the policy model, while retaining a source-of-truth check for sensitive results.
tradeoffs.caution: Stale permissions can become a data-leak path if index updates are treated as authoritative.

tradeoffs.title: Lexical, vector, or hybrid retrieval
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with the retrieval method that matches the corpus and latency budget, then add hybrid ranking behind an experiment and rollback boundary.
tradeoffs.caution: Adding embeddings without freshness, explainability, or access-control design increases cost without improving user trust.

commonMistakes: Returning ai powered semantic search engine results from an index generation whose ACL snapshot is stale.
Mutating the live index in place and exposing partially reindexed data.
Using offset pagination so inserts and deletes reorder later result pages.
Ignoring tombstones, deletes, or source-version gaps during replay.
Optimizing click-through while omitting tail latency, zero-result rate, and abusive-query controls.

followUps.question: How do you prevent a stale ai powered semantic search engine index from leaking data?
followUps.answer: Carry ACL or tenant versions through the document and query path, reject unsafe generations, and fail closed for sensitive filters.

followUps.question: How do you rebuild without downtime?
followUps.answer: Build a shadow generation from a source watermark, validate counts and permissions, then swap an alias atomically and retain the previous generation for rollback.

followUps.question: How do you debug an irrelevant result?
followUps.answer: Persist the query normalization, candidate set, rank features, model version, generation, and privacy-safe feedback trace.
